# listPersonNotes — GET /people/{vanId}/notes

List a person's notes

## Verified behaviors

- **Creating a note returns nothing — the id has to be read back** — Success is a bare 204: no body, no Location header, no noteId. The only way to learn the new id is GET /people/{vanId}/notes. The read-back also shows `isPinned` was accepted and ignored, and that an uncategorized note reads as the `{noteCategoryId: 0, name: null}` stub. ([replay](../behaviors/note-create-is-silent.md))
- **$orderby and $expand are validated, then change nothing** — `$orderby=CreatedDate desc` and `$expand=noteDetails` both pass validation and both return a body identical to the plain request — the sort never reorders and the expand never populates `contactHistory`. Values outside the accepted sets are refused with INVALID_PARAMETER, so the parameters are checked strictly and then ignored. ([replay](../behaviors/notes-list-tuning-parameters-are-inert.md))
- **A view-restricted note can be written but never read back** — `isViewRestricted: true` is accepted with the same 204 as any other note, and the note is then withheld from API keys entirely: absent from items and not counted in count, so every note the API ever shows has the flag false. ([replay](../behaviors/restricted-notes-vanish-from-the-api.md))

## Behavior

Returns the person's notes in the standard pagination envelope.

View-restricted notes are withheld from API keys: a note saved with `isViewRestricted: true` is absent from `items` and is not counted in `count`, so every note in the response has `isViewRestricted` false. `contactHistory` is always null, even for a note created with one, and `$expand=noteDetails` — the only value the parameter accepts — returns a byte-identical body.

Items come back oldest first by `createdDate`, ties broken by descending `noteId`. `$orderby` is validated against its two allowed properties but has no observable effect: `CreatedDate desc` returns the same order as the default.

An unknown, zero or negative vanId returns the standard 404 envelope; a non-integer path segment matches no route and returns an HTML 404 page.

## Differs from the official docs

- **parameters / vanId** — Official docs type this path parameter as string (default "100476252"); the route only matches integers — a non-integer segment returns an IIS HTML 404 page (observed 2026-08-04).

## Example

```bash
curl -sS -X GET \
  'https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714507/notes?$top=25' \
  -u "app-name:$NGP_API_KEY|1"
```

| Name | Type | Notes |

## Query parameters

| Name | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$top` | integer (int32) | Limits the number of results. Default 25, maximum 50. A value of 0 or less returns 400; so does a non-numeric value, with the same message as an over-maximum one. |
| `$skip` | integer (int32) | Number of results to skip. Must be 0 or greater. |
| `$orderby` | string | Accepted but ignored. The API validates the value — only `CreatedDate` and `IsPinned` pass, case-insensitively, optionally followed by ` desc` — and then returns the default order regardless, including for `desc`. One of: `CreatedDate`, `CreatedDate desc`, `IsPinned`, `IsPinned desc`. |
| `$expand` | string | `noteDetails` is the only value the API accepts; anything else returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with a hint saying so. Expanding has no observable effect — the response is identical with and without it, `contactHistory` included. One of: `noteDetails`. |

`*` = required.
